batchName: Roman Religion and Mythology (753 BC-AD 391) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: What did the Roman goddess Ceres watch over?
questions.explanation: Roman gods had practical jobs: Ceres guarded the growing grain, while Pomona looked after the fruit.
questions.sourceQuote: Janus guarded the door and Vesta the hearth, Ceres watched over the growing grain and Pomona the fruit.

questions.question: Who acted as the priest of a Roman household?
questions.explanation: The paterfamilias made the daily offerings, while his wife looked after the worship of Vesta at the hearth.
questions.sourceQuote: The father of the family (*paterfamilias*) acted as its priest, making daily offerings, while his wife looked after the worship of Vesta at the hearth.

questions.question: How many Vestal Virgins tended the sacred flame of Vesta?
questions.explanation: Six Vestals kept the flame of Vesta, goddess of the state hearth. Any household could rekindle its own fire from theirs.
questions.sourceQuote: The Vestals (*virgines Vestales*) were Rome's most famous priesthood: six women who tended the sacred flame of Vesta, goddess of the hearth of the Roman state.

questions.question: Whom did the emperor blame for the Great Fire of Rome in AD 64?
questions.explanation: The emperor blamed the Christians for the fire, and persecution followed. Roman officials saw their faith as atheism and dangerous superstition.
questions.sourceQuote: After the Great Fire of Rome in AD 64, the emperor Nero blamed the Christians, and persecution followed.

questions.question: The doors of the Temple of Janus were closed when Rome was...
questions.explanation: Janus was the two-faced god of doorways. His temple's doors stood open in wartime and stayed shut throughout Numa's peaceful reign.
questions.sourceQuote: Its doors stood open in wartime and closed in peace.

questions.question: Who were the Lares, honoured at every Roman home shrine?
options: Guardian spirits of house and fields
questions.explanation: The Lares guarded house and fields. They shared the home shrine with the Penates, who were gods of the household stores.
questions.sourceQuote: Every home had a shrine to the Lares, guardian spirits of house and fields, and the Penates, gods of the household stores.

questions.question: According to legend, which goddess was the mother of the Trojan prince Aeneas?
questions.explanation: Aeneas, son of Venus, escaped the fall of Troy and sailed to Italy. He brought sacred objects with him, including the Palladium.
questions.sourceQuote: The Trojan prince Aeneas, son of the goddess Venus, escaped and sailed to Italy carrying sacred objects, including the household gods of Troy and the Palladium, a holy statue said to protect a city.

questions.question: After a Roman emperor died, which body could vote to make him a god (divus)?
questions.explanation: The Senate could deify a dead emperor. The resulting imperial cult gave the empire a shared loyalty and made refusing to take part look like treason.
questions.sourceQuote: After his death, the Senate could vote him a god (*divus*).

questions.question: Who is the only Roman known to have been treated as a god while still alive?
questions.explanation: Julius Caesar was treated as a living god and was murdered soon after. He also claimed descent from Venus through Aeneas.
questions.sourceQuote: He is the only Roman known to have been treated as a god while still alive, and he was murdered soon after.

questions.question: In the traditional list of Rome's kings, where did the priest-king Numa come?
questions.explanation: Numa was the peaceful second king, and Romans traced most of their religious institutions back to him.
questions.sourceQuote: Romans believed that most of their religious institutions went back to Numa, the peaceful second king of Rome.
